newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan rebels say they fighting on edge of Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Afghan rebels say they fighting on edge of Kabul.

text.p: The Afghan Taleban militia said its forces had reached the eastern outskirts of Kabul on Wednesday and were battling government forces there.
Taleban sources quoted by the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said the rebels had captured Pul-i-Charki village on the eastern outskirts of the capital and the military academy.
Government sources in Kabul confirmed the Taleban were on the eastern edge of the city, but told AIP its troops still controlled the military academy.
The Taleban said fighting had moved on to the customs house area, only five km (three miles) from the city itself.
Government jets were bombing the Taleban, who were attacking Kabul from the east, south and southwest, the sources said.
The Islamic rebels made a lightning thrust up the main Jalalabad-Kabul highway after capturing the strategic town of Sarobi, 70 km (44 miles) from Kabul, overnight.
No independent account of the fighting was immediately available.
The latest Taleban advances followed a series of spectacular gains in eastern Afghanistan this month and put the survival of President Burhanuddin Rabbani's government in doubt.

Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, who rejoined the government in May under a peace deal with Rabbani, has since lost virtually all the territory previously controlled by his Hezb-i-Islami faction, including Sarobi.
The government, hemmed in by the latest Taleban advances, turned to opposition militia commander General Abdul Rashid Dostum, who controls Kabul's last supply route to the north.
An Islamabad-based official of Dostum's Jumbish-i-Milli faction said Interior Minister Yunus Qanuni was holding talks with Dostum in Uzbekistan's capital Tashkent on Wednesday.
He said Dostum had left for Tashkent four days ago for medical treatment. Qanuni had joined him there on Tuesday.
Mohammad said he had no information about the talks, but said Dostum would not support any Taleban attack on Kabul.

Dostum is an opponent of Rabbani, but is despised by the Taleban for his communist background. Last month he agreed to reopen the strategic Salang highway linking Kabul with the north as part of a truce with government forces.
The Taleban seized Sarobi at about midnight (1900 GMT Tuesday) in a two-pronged assault after resistance died away, Taleban sources in the Pakistani city of Peshawar said.
"Sarobi has been taken over completely," one source said. "Now, inshallah (God willing), we will reach Kabul."
The Islamic rebels have tightened their grip on eastern provinces this month as part of a drive to seize Kabul, oust Rabbani and impose a strict Islamic order across Afghanistan.
The Afghan government has often accused Pakistan of supporting the Taleban. Islamabad denies the charge.

Two government jets dropped at least three bombs on the Taleban-held airport at Jalalabad on Wednesday, but failed to damage airport buildings, Taleban sources said. A government plane dropped cluster bombs near the airport on Tuesday.
On Tuesday, the government-run radio said rockets fired by the Taleban killed three civilians and wounded nine in Kabul.
